items.excerpt: Koei Tecmo unveils an 'AI chat RPG' built on Atelier Ryza, where an LLM drives free-form conversation with the character instead of authored dialogue trees. A mainstream publisher shipping generative dialogue as the product, not a demo.
items.title: Game Company Reveals ‘Ai Chat RPG’ That’s Basically an Anime Girlfriend Simulator

items.excerpt: TheGamer's read on the same reveal: the Atelier Ryza chat RPG runs on AI at runtime, but Koei Tecmo stresses no generative AI was used to make the game's art or assets. The split between AI-as-feature and AI-as-production-tool is now an explicit positioning choice.
items.title: Atelier Ryza Is Getting An AI-Powered Chat RPG

items.excerpt: Diversion pitches a version-control layer rebuilt for AI coding agents and mixed code/binary game projects, arguing studios shouldn't have to choose between Git-style tooling and artist-friendly asset workflows. Pipeline plumbing is where AI adoption actually breaks.
items.title: Here's Why Game Studios Are Moving Beyond Legacy Version Control

items.excerpt: Shift Up's CEO argues the AI music video is fine because Evie was human-designed first, and PC Gamer explains why that defence misses the objection. A live case study in how studios justify generative AI in marketing craft.
items.title: Stellar Blade boss completely misses the point of why people are upset with Blood Rain's AI slop video: 'The AI is not creating [Evie] from scratch'

items.excerpt: Shift Up CEO Kim Hyung-tae asks players to 'view the work with that understanding in mind,' framing the AI video as an experiment layered on existing human designs.
items.title: 'View the Work With That Understanding in Mind' — Shift Up CEO Defends Stellar Blade: Blood Rain AI Music Video Against Player Backlash

items.excerpt: Kotaku on the backlash loop: the CEO's defence of the AI-generated promo video hardened fan opposition rather than settling it, a reminder that how you disclose AI is itself a design decision.
items.title: CEO Defends Stellar Blade 2 Slop Video And Makes Fans Angrier

items.excerpt: Eurogamer's account of Shift Up's response to the AI-generated Blood Rain music video, with the studio boss asking fans to judge the work 'with understanding in mind.'
items.title: "We would truly appreciate it if you could view the work with understanding in mind" - Shift Up CEO defends Stellar Blade: Blood Rain's AI music video as online backlash grows

items.excerpt: GamesRadar frames the dispute as a question of provenance: the studio says the character was human-authored head to toe, fans say the AI-generated motion and rendering is exactly what they object to.
items.title: Stellar Blade: Blood Rain studio CEO defends AI music video because Evie was originally "created from head to toe" by the devs, but fans say that's not the point

items.excerpt: Klang's decade-in-development MMO Seed ships LLM-driven avatars, and PC Gamer finds the conversations useful as a tutorial layer but corrosive to immersion. A rare in-the-wild verdict on generative NPC dialogue as shipped design.
items.title: MMO life sim Seed's AI-powered avatars prove once again that nothing shatters immersion quicker than crappy chatbot dialogue

items.excerpt: A static recompilation of Mario Kart Wii for PC admits AI was used 'for code' but not for art or assets, and the fan community rejected it anyway. Vibe coding is running into a credibility problem inside modding culture.
items.title: Mario Kart Wii is being "rebuilt for PC," but the project's AI vibe coding instantly soured many Nintendo fans on the project

items.excerpt: Nexus Mods splits its single generative-AI label into three so users can filter mods by which part of the work was AI-made. Granular disclosure taxonomy is becoming a real UX problem for creative platforms.
items.title: Nexus Mods update their generative AI-made mod tagging policy, dividing one label into three for more specific search filtering

items.excerpt: Aftermath interviews workers quietly dodging, misdirecting and sabotaging their employers' AI mandates: sarcastic compliance, meeting boycotts, silent reversion to old methods. The internal politics of top-down AX rollouts, from the floor.
items.title: Welcome To The Resistance: Meet The Workers Dodging (And Sabotaging) Their Employer's AI Mandates

items.excerpt: New EU deepfake rules put fresh constraints on games depicting real people and real places, with direct consequences for likeness capture, digital doubles and AI-assisted asset pipelines.
items.title: Why new EU deepfake legislation means games need to be careful when featuring real-world people and locations

items.excerpt: Reforged Labs, which sold AI-generated game ad creative, shuts down saying the gap it sold into is closing as platforms absorb the capability. A signal about which AI creative services survive as features rather than products.
items.title: AI startup Reforged Labs shuts down as the "gap we were selling into is closing"

items.excerpt: Square Enix pairs Dragon Quest with Google's Gemini for an in-person Tokyo event, one of the first big JRPG IP collaborations built around a consumer AI assistant rather than an in-game system.
items.title: Dragon Quest announces new collaboration with Google's Gemini for in-person event in Tokyo after DQX's controversial AI-powered companion

items.excerpt: With no GTA 6 gameplay trailer in sight, AI-generated fake footage is pulling millions of views: a case study in how generative video fills an information vacuum and shapes expectations of a game's visual identity.
items.title: As Grand Theft Auto 6 hopefuls grow anxious for a gameplay trailer, AI GTA 6 slop is getting millions of views on social media
